title: Grateful Dead Live at Action House on 1970-11-09

ai_review.summary: Patchy audience tape of the mysterious 1970 Action House show – great moments like Attics of My Life and Deep Elem Blues, but marred by very poor sound quality.
ai_review.review: The performance shines with a gorgeous rendition of “Attics of My Life,” a funky, soulful “Deep Elem Blues,” and an upbeat “Walkin’ the Dog,” showing why those New York ’70 shows are beloved. Unfortunately the recording is an uneven audience capture – often wretched, with drop‑outs and variable fidelity that makes large sections hard to enjoy. Listeners who can look past the audio will find a rare glimpse of a lost show, but most will struggle with the technical mess.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is praised (standout songs, energetic performance) while recording quality is repeatedly described as poor or wretched; weighted average of these factors yields an overall middling rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Often described as wretched, muddy, and with drop‑outs; quality varies wildly between tracks, likely a compilation of audience tapes from different dates rather than a single coherent board recording.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers note the tape is a patchwork of selections rather than a full set, but the included songs flow well and capture the high‑energy vibe typical of 1970 New York shows.

band_member_comments.Phil: His bass on “Deep Elem Blues” is described as jack‑hammer‑like and driving.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s second‑guitar work (referred to as ‘young Robert Weir’) shines on the deep blues numbers.
